title: Design a Booking System (Ticketmaster / BookMyShow, seat locking)
relevance: High — canonical HLD for contention + inventory; campus + FAANG / Indian product cos (Amazon, Flipkart, Uber, Atlassian, BookMyShow-style rounds); also maps to hotels/airlines.
company_notes: Very common campus/intern/new-grad HLD as BookMyShow/Ticketmaster/movie booking (seat lock, payment window, basic scale); at 1–4 YOE depth shifts to waiting rooms, Redis vs DB correctness, payment sagas/idempotency, hot-event isolation, bot/fairness; among the top contention/inventory HLD prompts alongside URL shortener and rate limiter.

phases.goal: Lock FRs/NFRs: two-phase hold+confirm, no double-booking, AP browse vs CP booking, hold TTL, and onsale-scale assumptions.

must_hit.point: Core FRs: browse/search events, view seat map + availability, select and hold seats, pay and confirm booking, view confirmation/ticket.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists browse → seat map → hold → pay/confirm → ticket without collapsing hold and confirm into one step.

must_hit.point: NFRs: never double-book; hold+confirm strongly consistent (CP); browse/search AP with stale seat map OK for seconds; hold window ~10 min; survive onsale spikes with millions concurrent; search latency ≪ 500 ms; read-heavy outside onsale.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States CAP split by path and names no-double-booking plus time-bound hold before diving into boxes.

must_hit.point: Clarify scope: movie shows vs concerts, assigned seats vs GA, peak QPS, hold TTL, whether payment is in-scope; optional FRs include cancel/refund, waitlist, dynamic pricing, admin events, multi-city aggregator, Verified Fan/bot gates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks clarifying questions and marks optional features instead of silently designing everything.

probes: What must never happen on the booking path, and how does browse consistency differ from hold/confirm?

hints.1: Start with the user journey from finding an event to holding a seat and paying.
hints.2: Separate browse/search availability from the atomic hold+confirm path in your NFRs.
hints.3: Say AP for browse (stale map OK briefly), CP/strong consistency for hold+confirm, hold ~10 min, no double-booking, search ≪ 500 ms.

phases.goal: Show browse-heavy steady state vs onsale spike, finite inventory, and why cache/waiting room/Redis holds beat a bigger SQL box.

must_hit.point: Steady state: e.g. 100M DAU × 100 req/user/day drives huge browse QPS; booking writes ≪ reads (~100:1 outside onsale).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States assumptions out loud and contrasts read-heavy browse with far fewer booking writes.

must_hit.point: Onsale spike: one popular event with 50k–100k seats can draw millions concurrent at T0 (Taylor Swift-class ~14M users / ~3.5B requests); confirm rate may only be thousands/min so a queue must absorb the rest.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates concurrent arrival from seats sold and concludes admission control is required.

must_hit.point: Storage: venues/events small; per-seat ticket rows dominate — e.g. 1k cities × 5 venues × 1k seats × 2 shows/day is tens of millions of seat-rows/year; booking rows ~100 B each.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Roughs seat-row scale and implies inventory/locking design matters more than raw DB size.

probes: Walk through back-of-envelope for steady browse vs a blockbuster onsale — where do the writes actually go?

hints.1: State DAU/read assumptions, then contrast with one hot event at T0.
hints.2: Compare seat inventory size to concurrent users trying to book.
hints.3: Use ~100:1 reads:writes outside onsale; onsale ~14M users / multi-billion requests; queue absorbs excess beyond confirm capacity.

phases.goal: Define hold then confirm APIs with conflict semantics, auth ownership, and idempotent booking.

must_hit.point: POST /events/{eventId}/holds with seatIds returns holdId + expiresAt; 409 if any seat taken; POST /bookings with holdId + paymentMethodId returns bookingId + tickets and is idempotent.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Two-phase endpoints: reserve/hold first, confirm after payment, with 409 on conflict.

must_hit.point: Also expose GET /events/{eventId}, GET /events/search, and optionally DELETE /holds/{holdId}, GET /bookings/{bookingId}, GET /queue/{eventId}; auth user from token — never trust userId in body for hold ownership.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Covers browse/search plus auth binding holds to the authenticated user.

probes: What does the hold API return on success vs when another user already took a seat?

hints.1: Think reserve-then-confirm rather than a single book-and-pay call.
hints.2: Hold creates a timed reservation; booking confirms after payment with conflict status codes.
hints.3: POST holds → holdId/expiresAt or 409; POST bookings idempotent with holdId; ownership from auth token.

phases.goal: Model event/venue/ticket/booking with AVAILABLE→HELD→BOOKED, uniqueness fences, and Redis TTL holds.

must_hit.point: ticket has status ENUM available/held/booked, hold_id, hold_expires_at, version; UNIQUE(event_id, section, row, seat); booking_seat UNIQUE(ticket_id) as final no-double-sell; Redis key seat:{eventId}:{ticketId} = owner with TTL 600s.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows state machine fields plus DB unique constraint and Redis ephemeral hold key with TTL 600s.

must_hit.point: event and venue tables hold metadata/seat_map; index (event_id, status) for seat-map queries; search often offloaded to Elasticsearch via CDC; payment intents/idempotency keys stay off the seat-map hot path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates catalog/search from hot inventory and names indexing/CDC for search.

probes: How do you represent seat state and guarantee the same seat cannot be sold twice at the DB layer?

hints.1: Start from event/venue/ticket/booking entities and seat status.
hints.2: AVAILABLE → HELD → BOOKED with time-bound hold fields and a uniqueness constraint on sold seats.
hints.3: ticket status + hold_expires_at + UNIQUE seat + booking_seat UNIQUE(ticket_id); Redis seat:{event}:{ticket} TTL 600s.

phases.goal: Sketch client→edge→services with waiting room, Redis holds, Postgres as truth, and async notifications.

must_hit.point: Client → CDN/Edge → LB/API Gateway → Search (Elasticsearch), Event Service (cache + Events DB, AP-friendly reads), optional Waiting Room (Redis ZSET) with admit token, Booking Service → Redis seat locks → Tickets/Bookings DB (Postgres) → Payment Gateway; async queue to notification/PDF workers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws browse vs booking paths, waiting room before hold, and async off confirm.

must_hit.point: Stateless app tier; Booking fleet sized for admitted users only; Postgres (ACID) is source of truth for sold seats; Redis is ephemeral holds + queue — efficiency layer, not sole correctness.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly says DB is truth for sold seats and Redis holds/queue are ephemeral.

probes: Where does the waiting room sit relative to the hold API, and what is the source of truth for a sold seat?

hints.1: Split read-heavy event browse from write-heavy booking.
hints.2: Put admission control in front of booking; keep notifications off the confirm path.
hints.3: Waiting room admits tokens into Booking → Redis locks → Postgres truth; queue workers for tickets/notifications.

phases.goal: Defend double-booking prevention, Redis vs DB holds, waiting room vs blind scale, and locking strategy on confirm.

must_hit.point: Prevent double-booking with Redis SET NX EX hold plus short DB txn on confirm (UNIQUE(ticket_id) or UPDATE … WHERE status='held' AND hold_id=?); multi-minute SELECT FOR UPDATE while user pays is wrong; refund if TTL races payment.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names SET NX EX + DB fence and rejects holding row locks across payment.

must_hit.point: Hold in Redis vs DB status+expires_at: Redis gives auto TTL + speed; DB-only is simpler but needs sweeper/lazy reclaim; hybrid Redis TTL + write-through held flag is a common senior answer; Redis alone is not truth (Kleppmann/Redlock caveats).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares Redis TTL, DB status, and hybrid; cites Redis as efficiency with DB correctness.

must_hit.point: Waiting room vs horizontal scale: finite contended inventory — more servers do not create more seats; admission + fairness beat blind autoscale; mega onsales need the queue before the seat map. Multi-seat holds must be all-or-none.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Argues admission control for finite seats and atomic multi-seat acquisition.

probes: How do you prevent two users from booking the same seat, and why not hold SELECT FOR UPDATE until payment finishes?

hints.1: Focus on the atomic hold and what happens at confirm.
hints.2: Contrast long DB row locks with short txn + TTL hold + uniqueness fence.
hints.3: SET NX EX hold, confirm with conditional UPDATE/UNIQUE; Redis not sole truth; waiting room before map for mega onsales.

phases.goal: Scale onsale herd, hot event shards, seat-map reads, and payment/notification failure modes without blocking confirm.

must_hit.point: Onsale thundering herd: waiting room + edge rate limits + bot mitigation so millions do not hit the hold API; partition inventory by event_id/show_id and protect the inherently hot shard with queue + Redis, not infinite SQL connections.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names waiting room/rate limits and event-scoped partitioning for hot onsales.

must_hit.point: Seat-map read QPS via CDN/cache of event+venue with careful availability overlay (short TTL / Redis / SSE); never block confirm on email/SMS — queue workers; extend hold TTL when payment starts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Caches catalog aggressively, keeps availability advisory, and moves notifications async.

must_hit.point: Failure modes: Redis down → degrade or fail-closed on hold but keep DB uniqueness; payment success + booking fail → reconcile + refund; expired hold after charge → refund; search via Elasticsearch+CDC not LIKE on primary.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks Redis outage, payment/booking mismatch, and search offload without inventing extra figures.

probes: What breaks first in a Taylor Swift-class onsale, and how do you keep the confirm path short?

hints.1: Think about millions arriving for one event's finite seats.
hints.2: Protect the hot event path before the DB and keep side effects async.
hints.3: Waiting room + event_id partition + Redis holds; async notifications; DB uniqueness survives Redis loss; refund/reconcile on payment races.

tradeoffs.topic: Long SELECT FOR UPDATE while user pays vs short DB txn + TTL hold
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Holding row locks across minutes of user payment is bad (ties up DB connections); prefer status+expires_at with short transactions/lazy reclaim, or Redis SET NX EX for speed + auto-expiry, with DB unique/OCC as final safety net.

tradeoffs.topic: Redis seat lock vs DB status columns (vs hybrid)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Redis: auto TTL and speed for holds; DB status: simpler single store but needs sweeper or lazy expiry; hybrid Redis TTL + write-through held flag is a common senior answer — Redis remains an efficiency layer, Postgres/conditional write rejects double-sell.

tradeoffs.topic: Waiting room vs just scaling horizontally
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Inventory is finite and contended — more servers do not create more seats; controlled admission (Redis ZSET FIFO or Queue-it-style) plus fairness beats blind autoscale for bots/cost; mega onsales need the queue before the seat map.

tradeoffs.topic: Optimistic vs pessimistic locking on confirm
tradeoffs.strong_answer: OCC/version under moderate contention; under blockbuster contention, fail fast on hold acquisition (SET NX) and keep the confirm transaction tiny.

tradeoffs.topic: CP booking path vs AP browse/search
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Browse/search/event page can be AP with briefly stale seat maps; hold+confirm must be CP/strong consistency so the same seat is never sold twice.

gotchas.trap: Two users click the same seat at once — unclear winner or last-write-wins.
gotchas.correction: Atomic hold (SET NX / conditional DB update); loser gets 409; seat map should refresh.

gotchas.trap: User closes the tab mid-checkout and seat stays locked forever.
gotchas.correction: TTL expiry releases the seat; no dependency on client unload.

gotchas.trap: Payment succeeds after hold expired and someone else booked.
gotchas.correction: Confirm txn fails; automatic refund; ideally extend the lock when payment begins.

gotchas.trap: Assuming Redlock is required for correctness.
gotchas.correction: Usually no for interviews; single Redis + DB fence is the expected answer; know Kleppmann’s critique if pushed — Redis/Redlock alone is not a correctness fence.

gotchas.trap: Treating GA/quantity inventory like assigned seats without atomicity.
gotchas.correction: Use counter/DECR with floor at 0 (still atomic) vs per-seat keys; same two-phase hold idea.

gotchas.trap: BookMyShow-style aggregator ignoring theatre channel inventory.
gotchas.correction: Aggregator uses reserved allotment or live theatre API; still need local hold TTL so the seat is blocked across channels for ~10 min.

gotchas.trap: Drawing a cache of available seats as source of truth.
gotchas.correction: Cache is advisory; interviewer will force a double-book scenario — only atomic hold + DB uniqueness prevent double-sell.
